data.narrative:
Andromeda Surgical is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Nick Damiano and Kartik Tiwari that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit, Recursion Pharmaceuticals, and Freenome.

Three standard triangulation methods were evaluated. Stage-progression analysis was rejected because the implied $7.5B valuation (applying a 2.5x multiplier to a $3.0B base) exceeded 20x the company's total capital raised, indicating an unreliable base value. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within the seed cohort; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met the filter threshold of three or more datapoints at matching stage or valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring could not proceed because target revenue is not disclosed—a common constraint for private companies—and applying the sector P/S median of 6.6x requires known revenue figures.

Given these constraints, a reliable triangulated valuation range cannot be supported from the available data. The analysis is limited by the absence of comparable seed-stage transactions with disclosed valuations in the surgical biotech subsector, lack of target revenue data, and a public comp set too small (n=3) to anchor a confident multiple. Further information on comparable seed rounds or early revenue would be required to establish a defensible valuation.
